record.original_question: Consider multi-frequency group synchronization over SO(2) or over a finite group, with signal elements sampled uniformly from the group and observed through L frequency channels. Determine a scaling L = L_n such that there exists a polynomial-time algorithm that reliably detects the signal as n -> infinity for all signal strengths lambda > lambda_comp,L with lambda_comp,L < 1.

evidence.quote: Open Problem 7. Consider synchronization model over SO(2) or synchronization model over a finite group, where the signal x is sampled uniformly over group elements. Find a scaling L = Ln of number of frequencies such that there exists a polynomial-time algorithm that can detect the signal reliably for all λ > λcomp,L for some λcomp,L < 1 as n → ∞.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $G$ be either the rotation group $SO(2)$ or a fixed finite group, and let $\{\rho_\ell\}_{\ell\ge 1}$ be a complete list of its nontrivial irreducible unitary representations (the "frequency channels"), with $\rho_\ell : G \to U(d_\ell)$. Fix an integer $n\ge 1$ and let $x_1,\dots,x_n$ be i.i.d. uniformly random elements of $G$ (the hidden signal). For each frequency $\ell \in \{1,\dots,L\}$, one observes the $n\times n$ block matrix
$$Y^{(\ell)} \;=\; \frac{\lambda}{n}\, X^{(\ell)} (X^{(\ell)})^* \;+\; \frac{1}{\sqrt{n}}\, W^{(\ell)},$$
where $X^{(\ell)} \in \mathbb{C}^{n d_\ell \times d_\ell}$ has blocks $\rho_\ell(x_i)$, $W^{(\ell)}$ is an independent GUE-type Hermitian noise matrix at scale $\ell$, and $\lambda > 0$ is the signal-to-noise ratio. Under the null hypothesis the observations are pure noise; under the planted hypothesis they follow the model above. The detection task is to test the null against the planted hypothesis with vanishing total error as $n\to\infty$.

For a single frequency ($L=1$), the spectral (PCA) threshold is $\lambda=1$, and it is conjectured (and partially established) that no polynomial-time algorithm achieves reliable detection below this threshold. Allowing the use of $L$ frequency channels jointly, define $\lambda_{\mathrm{comp},L}$ as the infimum of $\lambda$ for which some polynomial-time test reliably detects the signal as $n\to\infty$.

Problem: Determine a scaling $L = L_n$ (as a function of $n$) for which there exists a polynomial-time algorithm (using the observations $Y^{(1)},\dots,Y^{(L_n)}$) that reliably detects the signal for all $\lambda > \lambda_{\mathrm{comp},L_n}$ with $\lambda_{\mathrm{comp},L_n} < 1$; equivalently, exhibit a sub-spectral computationally efficient detection threshold by using sufficiently many frequencies.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is stated as an open problem in a 2025 preprint on multi-frequency group synchronization. A brief web search did not surface a subsequent resolution providing a polynomial-time sub-spectral detector for $SO(2)$ or finite-group synchronization via frequency scaling; the problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.snippet: Open problem on finding a scaling L=L_n of frequencies allowing polynomial-time detection below the spectral threshold for SO(2) and finite-group synchronization.
status_evidence.claim: Stated as an open problem in 2025; no resolution found in subsequent literature.
